units.translation: the transmitted reading ⟦1⟧ cannot be retained and is not supported by the second scholion either: ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧. Accordingly van Herwerden ⟦6⟧, since the latter word, instead of ⟦7⟧, probably belonged to the explained reading. Hardly, however, ⟦8⟧, cf. ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧, but rather ⟦11⟧., cf. 726 ⟦12⟧, and especially 667 ⟦13⟧ . . ⟦14⟧ . . ⟦15⟧. Or ⟦16⟧ (⟦17⟧ Weckl. would prefer), cf. ⟦18⟧ ⟦19⟧, ⟦20⟧ Frg. 287, since ⟦21⟧ is not found in A. (⟦22⟧ namely ⟦23⟧), or also ⟦24⟧. On ⟦25⟧. cf. ⟦26⟧ ⟦27⟧. — On the matter see what is adduced in the scholia, and below on 451.

⟦1⟧ as in Plat. ⟦2⟧, 872 E ⟦3⟧ (scil. ⟦4⟧, of parricide), ⟦5⟧. Here, however, the ⟦6⟧ has been washed out (⟦7⟧) by ⟦8⟧ (cf. on 449 ff.); similarly Frg. 340, which will be from a tragedy about Ixion [Weckl.]). So cheaply? Does A. believe in it? He does not even let Orestes believe in it very much; for the latter appeals besides to the long time that has passed and to his many dealings with other people, here indeed as proof that he brings no pollution and therefore no longer has any, yet at V. 238 ff. and 451 f. as to something that likewise rubs off the stain, just as an actual bloodstain is gradually rubbed off. The Erinyes do not care about any of this in the slightest. But ritually Orestes is pure, i.e., he can speak and associate with anyone, which he was not allowed to do before the purification.
